setup.title: Connect your key
setup.lead: The assistant runs on your own key. When you send a message, your browser sends it, with the open project's data the assistant reads, straight to the provider you choose. Nothing passes through First Move's servers.

provider.label: Provider
provider.gatewayHint: The same key as the AI Plan Score: one key serves both.
provider.openrouterHint: One key for many models, with the Auto Router.

key.label: API key
key.invalid: This does not look like a key of this provider. Paste the whole key, without spaces.

where.gateway: Where to get a key: sign in to Vercel, open AI Gateway in your dashboard and create an API key there. The Gateway needs credits on your account before it runs a model.
where.openrouter: Where to get a key: sign in at openrouter.ai, open Keys and create a key there. OpenRouter needs credits on your account for paid models.

storage.label: Keep the key
storage.sessionHint: Recommended. The key stays in this tab's memory and is gone when you reload or close the tab.
storage.remember: Remember on this device with a PIN
storage.rememberHint: The key is encrypted in this browser under your six-digit PIN. Five wrong PINs delete it, and it locks after 30 minutes without use. The PIN stops other people who use this browser; it does not protect against someone who copies your browser profile or runs code in this page. The spending limit at your provider is the real safety net.

pin.label: Six-digit PIN
pin.common: This PIN is too easy to guess. Choose another.
pin.mismatch: The two PINs are not the same.

setup.checking: Checking the key with the provider…
setup.failed: The key could not be checked. {reason}
setup.unavailable: This browser cannot keep the key on the device. It is used for this tab only.
setup.remembered: Remembered on this device under your PIN.
setup.limit: Credit limit of this key: {amount}, {remaining} left.
setup.noLimit: This key has no credit limit. Set one on the key at openrouter.ai/keys, or create a new key with a limit.
setup.noExpiry: OpenRouter reports no expiry date for this key. Create a key with an expiration, or delete this one when you are done.

model.label: Model
model.customInvalid: Use the form creator/model, for example {example}.
model.customHint: The model must support tool use. Its price is listed by your provider.
model.auto: Picks a model for each message and bills that model's price.

notice.title: Set a spending limit and an expiry date on the key
notice.lead: The assistant keeps the key safe in your browser, but the limit that really protects you is the one at your provider. Set both when you create the key:

gateway.limit: Spending limit: in the Create key dialog of the AI Gateway API Keys page, turn on the budget option, enter a spending limit in dollars and choose a refresh period (daily, weekly, monthly or none). AI Gateway then rejects requests once the limit is exceeded. A budget is a soft cap: the request that crosses it still completes.
gateway.expiry: Expiry date: Vercel's docs offer an expiry only when you create the key with the Vercel CLI or API, for example vercel ai-gateway api-keys create --name first-move --limit 10 --expiration 30d (7d, 30d, 60d, 90d or 1y). A key created in the dashboard never expires until you delete it, so delete it when you no longer need it and create a new one.

openrouter.limit: Credit limit: when you create the key at openrouter.ai/keys, choose a credit limit and, if you like, a daily, weekly or monthly reset. Once the key has used its limit, OpenRouter rejects its requests. OpenRouter recommends a limit on every key.
openrouter.expiry: Expiry date: give the key an expiration date when you create it. The expiration of an existing key cannot be changed, so set it then.
openrouter.docs: OpenRouter docs: API keys and limits

notice.ack: I have set a spending limit and an expiry date on this key, or I will delete the key when I no longer need it.
notice.required: Confirm this before the key is used.

unlock.title: Unlock your remembered key
unlock.lead: Your {provider} key ending in {last4} is remembered on this device.
unlock.wrong: Wrong PIN. {remaining} attempts left before the key is deleted.
unlock.wiped: Too many wrong PINs: the remembered key has been deleted. Paste the key again.
unlock.missing: No remembered key was found. Paste the key again.
unlock.unavailable: This browser cannot open the remembered key.

chat.noProject: No project is open. You can still ask about First Move's method.
chat.empty: Ask about your open project or about how First Move calculates. For example:

examples.result: Why does my Quick Check show this result?
examples.length: How is the network length estimated?
examples.missing: What is still missing in my project?

chat.label: Message to the assistant

tools.explain: Looked up how First Move calculates

chat.privacy: Your messages, and the project data the assistant reads, go to {provider} under your key. AI answers can be wrong: check them against the results.

review.title: Proposed values
review.lead: Nothing changes until you apply. Applied values are marked as AI-proposed until you edit them.
review.conflict: Different values were found; none was picked
review.noProject: Open the project again to apply these values.

errors.key: The provider did not accept the key. Check that it is complete and still active.
errors.credits: The key's spending limit or your account's credits are used up. Raise the limit or add credits at your provider, then try again.
errors.forbidden: The key may not use this model. Check its settings at your provider, or choose another model.
errors.model: The provider does not offer this model, or not without collecting data, which the assistant does not allow. Choose another model.
errors.rate: Too many requests right now. Wait a minute, then try again.
errors.provider: The model provider had a problem. Try again in a moment.
errors.network: The provider could not be reached, or it took too long. Check your connection, then try again.
